title: First Overflow
summary: A visitor-badge printer copies your name into a buffer that is far too small. A hidden override function reads the vault.
objectives: Work out the distance to the saved return address
Redirect execution to the override function and read the vault
learningOutcomes: Explain how a stack buffer overflow overwrites a return address
Use gdb and pwntools to build a simple exploit
Describe the mitigations (canaries, non-executable stack, ASLR, bounds checks) that stop it

hints.bodyMd: The source is in `/opt/first-overflow/vuln.c`. `read()` takes more bytes than the `name` buffer holds. Build the same binary locally, or load the copy at `/opt/first-overflow/vuln` in gdb.

The binary is built with `-no-pie`, so `win()` is at a fixed address: `objdump -d vuln | grep win`. Overflow the buffer up to the saved return address, then place that address. If the program crashes inside `win()`, add one `ret` gadget before it to keep the stack 16-byte aligned.
